facts.text: Ahoskie began as a railroad siding in 1885, hauling timber from nearby forests to a sawmill at Tunis on the Chowan and Southern Railroad line.
The town grew around a loading station and supply stores for log workers, becoming a base for traveling salesmen who rode horse and buggy to surrounding communities.
Ahoskie’s nickname, "The Only One," comes from the fact that no other town in the world shares its unique name.
In 1889, Ahoskie established its post office, and the first passenger train arrived the next year on the newly opened Norfolk and Carolina line.
The town’s first bank, the Bank of Ahoskie, was chartered in 1905, marking a milestone in its early economic development.
Ahoskie hosts three historic districts—Ahoskie Historic District, Ahoskie Downtown Historic District, and East End Historic District—all listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
